pages.text: Shares represent part ownership of a listed company and are traded through licensed brokers on the exchange. Investors open a depository account to hold their shares in electronic form. Share prices move with company results, market sentiment and the wider economy. Companies may pay dividends out of profit, but they are not obliged to. The exchange publishes a daily price list and the all-share index summarises the market.

Share trades settle on T+3, that is three business days after the trade date. Brokerage commission on share trades may not exceed 1.2 percent of the trade value. This guide was issued by the SYN Securities Exchange for retail investors and is reviewed every year. Readers who need advice on shares should consult a licensed adviser, because this guide gives information only. [SYNTHETIC TEST DATA: fictional organisations and invented figures. Not real financial information.]
